name: Worship of the nine enclosures of the Śrīcakra (navāvaraṇa-pūjā)
method_summary: After the preliminaries (Gaṇapati worship, purification, placements on the body, preparation of the special water), the Goddess is invoked into the central point and the deities of the nine enclosures are worshipped from the outer square inward — each enclosure with its presiding goddess, class of yoginīs, attendant deities and mudrā — followed by the sixty-four services, libations into the bindu, japa and the offering of all to the Goddess. The Yoginīhṛdaya calls this cakra-worship 'aparā', performed even by Śiva; the Samaya school performs it only inwardly. (Summary; no mantras recorded.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The Kaula worship is to be done in secret; making it public leads to hell.
Outer worship on a physical support is rejected by the Samayins, who worship only in the heart-space.

equivalents.note: outer and inner forms of the same worship

name: Inner worship (antaryāga)
method_summary: Śrīvidyā contribution: the whole worship is performed within — knower as offerer, knowledge as fire, the known as oblation (Bhāvanā Upaniṣad; PKS 1.26); the Yoginīhṛdaya's inner worship suffices for those firm in it (Setubandha); the Samaya school worships only in the heart and crown.

name: Samaya worship in the heart-space (dahara)
method_summary: The Samayin imagines the Śrīcakra in the small space of the heart (or identifies it with the moon-disc in the crown lotus) and worships the Goddess there without any external support; he also worships the Śiva-Śakti pair in each cakra, Samayā with Samaya in the base and the thousand-petalled lotus (SL 36-41 with Lakṣmīdhara).
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

equivalents.note: the Samaya form of inner worship

name: Worship of the Goddess led through the cakras (Samaya procedure described by Bhāskararāya)
method_summary: When the initiate's contemplation of unity is firm and the guru's rite of 'great piercing' (mahāvedha) has been done, the Goddess, risen from the base, is said to become manifest in the maṇipūra; there she is worshipped with offerings, then led to the heart, the throat and the brow with further offerings, and united with Sadāśiva in the thousand-petalled lotus. Summary only — no method of raising the power is recorded.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā
firm contemplation of the unities; the guru's mahāvedha rite

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The mind's steady flow toward the meaning comes only by the guru's grace, not by scripture alone.

name: Contemplation of the Goddess as kuṇḍalinī
method_summary: Contemplation of the Goddess rising from the base through the cakras, piercing the three knots, uniting with her consort in the crown, showering nectar over the body and returning to sleep coiled at the base, as described in the Sahasranāma and the Saundaryalaharī; in the Kalpasūtra's morning routine the nectar flows from the guru's feet in the crown. Summary only.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The mind's steady flow toward the meaning comes only by the guru's grace, not by scripture alone.

signs_of_progress: nectar felt flowing from the crown (SL 10; LSN 39)
the Goddess seen as a streak of lightning above the six lotuses by the pure-minded (SL 21)

name: Contemplation of the body as the Śrīcakra (Bhāvanā Upaniṣad)
method_summary: Each part of the Śrīcakra and each deity is identified with a constituent of one's body and mind (channels, vital airs, fires, qualities, subtle elements, inner organ, lunar days); the offerings are made as inner acts; the worship is the contemplation of the non-difference of knower, knowing and known. Bhāskararāya wrote a procedure (prayoga) for it.
duration: three muhūrtas of absorption (as the Upaniṣad states)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā
signs_of_progress: identity with the deity; intentions fulfilled without effort; called a Śiva-yogin (Bhāvanā Upaniṣad)

name: Contemplation 'I am you' (identity with the Goddess)
method_summary: The worshipper contemplates himself as the Goddess ('I am you'), surrounded by her powers as rays of his own body (SL 96); in worship with the names the principal thing is to contemplate the identity of oneself and the deity (Bhāskararāya).

name: Japa of the Śrīvidyā mantra
method_summary: Repetition of the fifteen- or sixteen-syllable mantra received at initiation, with attention to its subtle final phases and its meanings; the Varivasyārahasya insists that japa without knowledge of meaning bears no fruit. (No syllables recorded.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Recitation without knowing the meaning bears no fruit and may do harm.
Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.

name: Śrīvidyā initiation (śāktī, śāmbhavī, māntrī)
method_summary: The guru, after his own worship, purifies the blindfolded disciple with the special water, contemplates the red and white feet on his head and a wave of light burning away his bonds, bathes him from a consecrated vessel, places the letters on his body, whispers the Bālā mantra and then the chosen mantra, gives his own pādukā and a name ending in '-ānandanātha', teaches the rules of conduct and makes the disciple his own self (PKS 1.34-43). Summary only.

name: Worship of the guru's feet (pādukā) and the circle of gurus
method_summary: Daily contemplation of the guru's feet in the crown with nectar flowing from them (PKS 2.2), recitation of the pādukā given at initiation, and worship of the lineage of gurus in their divine, perfected and human streams.

name: Placements on the body (nyāsa) in Śrīvidyā
method_summary: Placing of mantras and deities on the body before worship: the purification of the hands, the eight goddesses of speech on head, forehead, brows, throat, heart, navel, genitals and base, the mātṛkā, the great sixfold placement and others, by which the worshipper becomes the deity's body. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: The ten mudrās of Śrīvidyā worship
method_summary: Ten hand-seals shown in the worship of the Śrīcakra, one for each enclosure (sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī to sarvayoni) and the tenth, trikhaṇḍā. (Names only; forms not described.)

name: Libation into the bindu (bindu-tarpaṇa)
method_summary: Offering libations of the consecrated special water into the central point of the Śrīcakra to satisfy the Goddess (LSN 178); substances vary by mode (Kaula or with substitutes). Summary only.

name: The sixty-four services (catuḥṣaṣṭy-upacāra)
method_summary: The Goddess is served in imagination and act as a queen with sixty-four royal services — bath, anointing, garments, jewels, weapons, mounting the cakra, sitting on Kāmeśvara's lap, drink, betel, lights, parasol, fans, mirror and the rest (PKS 4.5; LSN 58); the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad interiorizes the services.

name: The daily routine of the Śrīvidyā initiate
method_summary: Rising before dawn, contemplating the guru's feet in the crown with nectar flooding the body, meditating on Gaṇapati in the heart, the morning ablutions and offerings, libations, and the day's worship (PKS 2.2); constant holding of the vidyā and immersion in Śiva-hood (PKS 1.17-18).

name: Worship of Mahāgaṇapati before the great vidyā
method_summary: Worship of Mahāgaṇapati with his five enclosures to remove obstacles before the worship of the great vidyā. Taught in section 2 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Worship of Śyāmā (Mantriṇī)
method_summary: Worship of Śyāmā/Rājamātaṅgī, Lalitā's minister, with her own cakra and enclosures. Taught in section 6 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Worship of Vārāhī (Daṇḍinī)
method_summary: Worship of Vārāhī, Lalitā's general, with her own cakra and enclosures. Taught in section 7 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Worship of Parā
method_summary: Worship of Parā, the supreme Goddess, according to its own sequence. Taught in section 8 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Fire offering in Śrīvidyā
method_summary: The fire rite: preparation of the fire and offerings to the Goddess and her retinue. Taught in section 9 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Worship of the Nityā of the lunar day
method_summary: Worship of the Nityā presiding over the current lunar day, the Nityās being the phases of time (Tantrarāja; Bhāvanā Upaniṣad). Summary only.

name: Recitation of the Lalitā Sahasranāma
method_summary: Daily recitation of the thousand names, often with the introductory and concluding parts; Bhāskararāya treats it as a daily duty that can also serve desired ends; the Rudrayāmala (as he quotes it) places name-recitation at the summit of a ladder of births leading to liberation while living.

warnings.text: The concluding section restricts the hymn to devotees of Lalitā (as summarized; low confidence).

name: Worship with the thousand names (nāma-arcana, kuṅkumārcana)
method_summary: Offering one flower (or vermilion) into the bindu with each name in the dative with 'namaḥ', after reciting the introductory part and the placements, contemplating the identity of oneself and the Goddess as the principal thing (Bhāskararāya on the phalaśruti).

name: Worship with the Triśatī
method_summary: Worship offering vermilion with each of the three hundred names of the Triśatī, which together unfold the fifteen syllables of the mantra.

name: Recitation of the Saundaryalaharī
method_summary: Recitation of the hundred verses as praise and worship; popular manuals attach to each verse a yantra, a method of recitation and a fruit.
notes: The verse-by-verse prayoga tradition is recorded from memory; source manuals not identified.

name: Recitation of the Devī Māhātmya (Saptaśatī, Caṇḍī-pāṭha)
method_summary: Recitation of the seven hundred verses of the Devī Māhātmya, preceded by its limbs — the Kavaca, Argalā and Kīlaka — with japa of the nine-syllable mantra, and followed by the three 'secrets' (rahasya); especially on the eighth, ninth and fourteenth lunar days and in Navarātri.

name: The Navarātri observance
method_summary: Nine nights of worship of the Goddess in autumn and spring, with recitation, worship of young girls and — in many traditions — one of the nine Durgās on each night; accompanied by vows and fasts according to ability.

warnings.text: Fasts are to be kept according to ability; prolonged fasting is recorded in summary only.

name: Worship of young girls as the Goddess (kumārī-pūjā)
method_summary: Young girls are honoured and fed as living forms of the Goddess, especially during Navarātri.

name: Worship of married women (suvāsinī-pūjā)
method_summary: Married women are honoured as the Goddess, who 'is pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs' (LSN 178).

name: All action as worship (ātmārpaṇa)
method_summary: Offering every act of daily life — speech, gesture, walking, eating, lying down — to the Goddess as a form of her worship, with the attitude of self-offering (SL 27).

name: Meditation on the kāmakalā
method_summary: Meditation on the Goddess's kāmakalā form — the point as face, the two points below and the triangle — taught in the Saundaryalaharī for the power to attract and in the Kāmakalāvilāsa as knowledge of the Śiva-Śakti union that liberates. Summary only.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: The sixty-four tantras aimed at particular powers beguile the world; the Goddess's own tantra aims at all the ends of life.

name: Worship with the five 'M's (pañcamakāra) — summary only
method_summary: In the Kaula mode, wine, meat, fish, grain or gesture, and union are used in secret worship as manifestations of the bliss that is Brahman's form (PKS 1.12); the right-hand and Samaya modes use substitutes or interior equivalents, and the Samaya school rejects the practice. No procedure is recorded here.

warnings.text: The Kaula worship is to be done in secret; making it public leads to hell.
Daily worship is to continue even when the five 'M's are unavailable.
Rejected by the Samaya school as outside the Vedic path.

name: The secret sacrifice (rahoyāga) — summary only
method_summary: A secret rite by whose sequence the Goddess is worshipped, with secret libations (LSN 83); its content differs by lineage and is not recorded here.

warnings.text: The Kaula worship is to be done in secret; making it public leads to hell.

name: Keeping the initiate's conduct (samaya)
method_summary: Observing the rules of the Kalpasūtra: no censure of other schools or persons, secrecy, constant remembrance of the vidyā, avoidance of the six passions, unsanctioned violence and theft, one guru, non-possessiveness, action without regard to fruit, fearlessness; outwardly Śaiva and among people Vaiṣṇava (Kaula Upaniṣad).

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
